name: SlotCraft — the picking-floor twin that scores your layout
one_liner: A browser-native 3D digital twin of a 100-slot forward-pick area, driven by 2,359 real November-2011 orders from UCI Online Retail II, where supervisors watch pickers walk real invoices, managers re-slot products (by hand or with a simulated-annealing optimiser) and are scored by replaying the identical orders on a chronological held-out half, pickers get a handheld pick-list view, and every stretch goal (batching, multi-picker congestion, heatmap, server-validated leaderboard) is measured by the same 300-line headless simulator.
why_it_wins: All four scouts rank 4.2 first or second, and my lens (finish every stretch goal as one coherent product) fits it better than any other PS because every stretch goal is a measured feature of the same simulate() function, not a bolt-on: batching, congestion, heatmap and leaderboard all reuse the aisle-graph routing core. Judges remember it because (1) the must-have IS the showpiece: a self-drawing cyan pick path with bloom, heat accumulating on racks, and a ghost picker racing the new layout against the old with counters diverging live; (2) every number on screen is produced by a headless replay of all orders (ms), the animation only illustrates it, and a chronological held-out half (Nov 16-30, 1,229 orders) scores every layout, so the improvement is measured not claimed, exactly the core-challenge sentence; (3) it is a product with roles, not a demo: Floor (supervisor), Studio (manager), Analytics (manager), Handheld (picker), Leaderboard with server-side re-simulation of submitted layouts (anti-cheat), CSV/JSON/PNG exports, share-by-URL layouts, and an in-app Methods panel that prints the data-cleaning counts (1,368 duplicates, 441 cancelled invoices, 283 non-product lines, 261 non-positive rows, 21.2 % line coverage) so Q&A has nothing to catch; (4) technical depth an OR judge recognises: exact Held-Karp routing on an aisle graph, Hall-1993 S-shape/largest-gap ablation, SA slotting with incremental delta evaluation that captures order affinity ABC ignores, savings-based batching, resource-constrained multi-picker congestion; (5) zero demo risk: fully static Vercel site, no LLM, no keys in the demo path, deterministic seeds, quality toggle for weak GPUs, FPS auto-downgrade; (6) low competition: three.js scares ML-heavy student teams, so the field is empty while 2.2/1.1/2.1 are crowded.
demo_script:
All numbers below are placeholders to be read live from the deployed app; never say a number that eval/results.md does not contain. Browser at 125 %, Performance Mode auto, backup MP4 on two laptops, local `npm run preview` open in a second window.

0:00-0:25 HOOK (slide 1-2). "Order pickers spend about half their shift walking, not picking (Tompkins et al. 2010). Where a product sits decides how far they walk. SlotCraft turns slotting into a scored game on real orders." QR codes: live URL + repo.

0:25-0:55 FLOOR VIEW, data-driven proof. Open live URL (static, loads <2 s). Camera flies from the dock down aisle C to a 3/4 isometric (drei CameraControls.setLookAt, 1.8 s). Top bar reads "UCI Online Retail II · November 2011 · 100 SKUs · 2,359 orders · coverage 21.2 % of pick lines". Click bay C-07: card shows StockCode 23084 RABBIT NIGHT LIGHT, 487 picks this month, 14.6 m from dock. Press Play: ticker "Invoice 581483 · 5 lines"; picker walks; the path draws itself ahead of him in cyan with bloom; metres and mm:ss tick. WOW 1: self-drawing path + live counters.

0:55-1:30 HEAT + CONGESTION (stretch 1 and 3). Speed slider to 30x: bays and floor tiles warm from blue to red as visits accumulate (InstancedMesh instanceColor). Pickers slider 1 -> 4: four pickers, two meet in aisle B, one flashes red "waiting 4.1 s"; KPI tiles update: throughput orders/h, % time waiting. Say: "aisle = single-lane resource, conservative, stated in Methods". WOW 2: heat memory + congestion flash, both computed by the headless sim (badge: "simulated 1,229 orders in 38 ms; animating 12/1,229").

1:30-2:35 STUDIO, the core challenge. Switch to Studio (2D slot map synced to the 3D). Press "ABC baseline": fast movers slide toward the dock (motion layout animation); KPI row: Legacy / ABC / You, on both halves. Drag RABBIT NIGHT LIGHT next to PAPER CHAIN KIT 50'S CHRISTMAS ("co-picked in N orders" chip appears). Press Replay: 3D shows the ghost picker (35 % opacity, wireframe) walking the OLD layout while the solid picker walks the NEW one on the same invoices; two odometers diverge: "Before 18.4 km · After 15.1 km · -18 %" (live values). WOW 3: the before/after race. Then press "AI optimise": SA runs 8 s in a Web Worker, the objective curve drops live, iterations counted, seed shown; result card: "SA beats ABC by X % in-sample, Y % held-out (Y < X, as expected)", and three "why" chips derived from the co-pick matrix.

2:35-3:10 BATCHING (stretch 2). Toggle "Cart: 4 orders, savings batching": picker now carries 4 order tags, one tour serves them; chart "distance per order: single vs FCFS-4 vs savings-4" animates; all from sim.

3:10-3:40 HANDHELD + LEADERBOARD. Open /handheld on the phone (QR on slide): the picker's RF-gun view: next bay, metres to go, route-ordered pick list, progress bar, synced to the same deterministic clock. Back on laptop: "Submit layout" -> toast "Verified: server re-simulated 1,229 held-out orders in 41 ms" -> row appears ranked under seeded "Legacy", "ABC", "SA" entries; copy share link.

3:40-4:20 EVIDENCE. Analytics tab: table Legacy/ABC/SA/Player x (opt half, held-out half) with total km and avg pick time per order (the PS's optional metric); routing policy ablation S-shape vs largest-gap vs optimal on the same layout; order-size histogram (median 5, p90 15, max 76); Methods panel listing geometry, 1.2 m/s, 8 s/line, 15 s/order dock, cleaning counts, split dates; "Export CSV" downloads per-order results; say "`npm run eval` reproduces every number here; results.md carries the commit hash".

4:20-4:50 LIMITATIONS (slide). Forward-pick area only (top-100 SKUs = 21.2 % of lines); single-level bays; no replenishment or inventory; congestion model is a stated simplification; invoices of a UK online gift retailer are a proxy for WMS pick orders; SA is a heuristic, not optimal; layout geometry is ours. No LLM anywhere, by design.

4:50-5:00 CLOSE. Team, module ownership, AI tools declared (Claude Code agents, human-reviewed), #NEXAI2026, links.
wow_visual: Scene (React Three Fiber 9.8.2 + drei 10.7.9 on three 0.186.1, WebGLRenderer, no WebGPU): a 25 m x 18 m floor, 5 aisles (A-E) with racks both sides, 10 bays per side = 100 pick faces, front/back cross-aisles, dock at the front-left. Racks: uprights/beams via drei <Instances> (2 draw calls); 100 bay boxes as one InstancedMesh with per-instance instanceColor driven by visit counts (blue->amber->red ramp, lerped each frame); floor tiles per graph edge as a second InstancedMesh coloured by traversal count (heat memory). Labels: drei <Text> (troika) only for hovered/selected bay plus short StockCodes at close LOD. Picker: capsule + cap + trolley box (Kenney CC0 character GLB optional, loaded lazily, never on the critical path), moved along the sim's polyline route with constant 1.2 m/s * speed multiplier; up to 4 pickers with distinct colours. Path: drei <Line> (Line2, 3 px) whose points slice grows with the picker, cyan, Bloom from @react-three/postprocessing 3.2.1 (luminanceThreshold 0.8, mipmapBlur), N8AO 2.0.1 halfRes, SMAA; "Performance mode" disables all post-processing and caps DPR at 1.0; auto-downgrade if measured FPS < 40 for 2 s; frameloop="demand" while paused. Ghost race: second PickerRig on the OLD layout rendered with 35 % opacity wireframe and dashed grey path while the solid picker walks the NEW layout on the same invoice sequence; the two odometers are read from precomputed cumulative-distance arrays of the headless sim (so counters are sim-exact, never animation-derived). Congestion: waiting picker gets a pulsing red ring (emissive + bloom) and a floating "waiting 4.1 s" <Html> label; the occupied aisle floor tints red. Camera: drei <CameraControls> (camera-controls 3.1.2) with presets Dock / Aisle / Iso / Top, fly-to on bay click via fitToBox(true); GSAP 3.15.0 not needed. UI: Tailwind 4.3.3, motion 14.5.0 for KPI counters (animate(0,total)) and the Studio's 2D slot map (SVG, layout animations on swap, drag-and-drop with click-to-swap fallback), ECharts 6.1.0 for KPI bars, SA objective curve, policy ablation, order-size histogram, congestion-vs-pickers line. Views: Floor, Studio, Analytics, Handheld (/handheld phone frame), Leaderboard, Methods. Total scene cost: ~6 draw calls for geometry + lines + labels; runs at 60 fps on an integrated GPU with post off.
wow_technical:
Core = src/sim (pure TypeScript, no DOM, ~600 lines, shared by the web app, two Web Workers, the Vercel leaderboard function, vitest tests and `npm run eval`).
1) Aisle graph: 51 nodes (50 aisle-row nodes at bay rows + dock; cross-aisle junctions folded as edges), edge lengths from geometry (bay pitch 1.2 m, aisle centre pitch 5.0 m, cross-aisles 3.0 m); all-pairs Dijkstra -> Float32Array[51*51]; each slot maps to its aisle-row node, so two SKUs facing each other cost 0 extra. Walking strictly follows aisles; polylines are emitted for rendering.
2) Per-order routing: unique stops deduped by node; exact Held-Karp bitmask DP for <= 11 stops (11^2 * 2^11 = 248k ops, ~0.3 ms); nearest-neighbour + 2-opt + Or-opt for larger orders (p90 = 15 lines, max 76, so ~10 % of orders take the heuristic path; stated). Alternative classical policies implemented for the ablation: S-shape traversal and largest-gap (Hall 1993), return. Tour = dock -> stops -> dock. Time = distance/1.2 + 8 s * lines + 15 s dock.
3) simulate(layout, orders, policy, params) -> totals + per-order traces; deterministic; 2,359 orders in ~30-60 ms; identical output on repeated runs (vitest asserts).
4) Slotting: legacy = catalogue order (StockCode ascending filling slots aisle by aisle from the dock, declared); ABC baseline = SKUs by pick count desc assigned to slots by dock distance asc (the required auto baseline); SA optimiser (Kirkpatrick 1983) in sa.worker.ts: state = permutation of 100 SKUs over 100 slots, move = swap two SKUs, objective = total replayed distance on the opt half (Nov 1-15, 1,130 orders), incremental delta by recomputing only orders containing either SKU (inverted index SKU->orders, ~120 orders/SKU, avg order ~5 lines so DP is microseconds), identical-stop-set orders merged with weights, T0 = mean |delta| of 200 random swaps, geometric cooling to 0.01*T0, time-boxed 8 s, mulberry32 seed shown; warm-started from ABC. This captures co-pick affinity (co-occurrence matrix 100x100 computed client-side) that ABC cannot; "why" chips cite the co-pick counts.
5) Batching (stretch): cart capacity 4 orders; FCFS batching vs Clarke-Wright-style savings batching (De Koster, Van der Poort & Wolters 1999): saving(A,B) = d(A)+d(B)-d(A u B) with union routed by the same DP; report distance per order and pick time per order.
6) Multi-picker congestion (stretch): time-stepped 0.25 s simulation with K in 1..4 pickers consuming the order queue in timestamp order; each aisle is a single-lane resource (capacity 1); a picker arriving at an occupied aisle waits at the cross-aisle; outputs throughput (orders/h), total/percent waiting time, per-aisle occupancy; deterministic.
7) Heatmap (stretch): bay-visit and edge-traversal counts from the same traces.
8) Leaderboard (stretch): POST /api/leaderboard {name, layout[100]} -> server validates permutation and RE-RUNS simulate() on the held-out half before storing {name, heldOutKm, optKm, hash} in Upstash Redis sorted set (localStorage fallback if the function is unavailable).
Metrics that prove it (all from `npm run eval`, written to eval/results.md with commit hash): total km and avg pick time per order for Legacy / ABC / SA / Player on the opt half AND the held-out half (PS optional metric); SA-vs-ABC gain in-sample vs held-out (expect held-out smaller: honesty); routing ablation S-shape vs largest-gap vs optimal on each layout; batching distance/order single vs FCFS-4 vs savings-4; congestion table K=1..4 (throughput, % waiting); SA run 3 seeds mean+-sd; determinism test (two replays byte-identical).
mvp_mapping:
M1 (pre-processing -> JSON): data/prep.py (Python 3.12, pandas 3.0.6, pyarrow 26.0.0), run once: `python -I data/prep.py --src online_retail_II.parquet --month 2011-11 --top 100 --out public/data/orders_2011-11.json`. Steps and the real counts measured tonight on the exact file: November 2011 = 84,711 rows -> drop exact duplicate rows (1,368) -> drop invoices starting with "C" (1,073 rows, 441 invoices) -> keep StockCode matching ^\d{5}[A-Za-z]{0,2}$ (drops 283 rows: POST 165, DOT 47, M 44, C2 24, BANK CHARGES 2, DCGSSGIRL 1) -> drop Quantity<=0 or Price<=0 (261 rows; note Quantity/Price are strings in the HF parquet, cast with to_numeric) -> one pick line per (Invoice, StockCode) with summed quantity = 80,378 pick lines, 2,751 orders, 2,933 SKUs -> top-100 SKUs by pick-line count (119-487 picks each; #1 23084 RABBIT NIGHT LIGHT 487) -> orders restricted to those lines: 2,359 orders (2,009 with >=2 lines), 17,037 lines = 21.2 % coverage, median 5 lines, p90 15, max 76 -> chronological split opt = Nov 1-15 (1,130 orders), test = Nov 16-30 (1,229). JSON = {meta (every count above + source, licence, split, prep commit), skus[{i, code, desc, picks, qty}], orders[{id, ts, lines[skuIdx], qty[]}], split{opt[], test[]}} ~400 KB gz; co-pick matrix computed client-side. All counts are displayed in the in-app Methods panel.
M2 (3D grid warehouse replaying orders with aisle-following walking and live counters): Floor view: racks/aisles/dock/1-4 animated pickers (see wow_visual); the picker follows the sim's polyline route along the aisle graph (never through racks, visibly), order ticker shows Invoice id and line count, bay click shows StockCode/description/picks from the JSON, live metres and mm:ss counters are read from the headless sim's cumulative arrays, speed 1x-50x, play/pause, policy badge ("optimal: exact <=11 stops, 2-opt beyond"), and a badge stating "all N orders simulated headlessly in X ms; animating k/N".
M3 (game mode with before/after and automatic baseline): Studio view: drag or click-to-swap SKUs between slots on a 2D map synced to the 3D; Replay re-runs the identical order list on the new layout and shows before/after total km, avg pick time per order and per-order deltas on both halves; "ABC baseline" button computes fast-movers-nearest-dock automatically and is always shown as a column to beat; the ghost-race visual plus KPI table Legacy / ABC / You; undo/redo; share link encodes the 100-byte permutation in the URL hash.
stretch_goals: Several pickers with congestion: K=1..4 pickers, aisle = single-lane resource, waiting measured and visualised (red ring, aisle tint), throughput and % waiting KPIs, congestion-vs-K chart in Analytics
Batch picking: cart of 4 orders, FCFS vs savings-based batch formation, one tour per batch, distance/order and pick-time/order compared with single-order picking, cart tags visible on the picker
Heatmap of rack visits (bay instanceColor) and floor traversal (edge tiles), with a 2D twin in Analytics and a 'reset heat' control

Leaderboard of player layouts, server-validated by re-simulating the submitted layout on the held-out half (Vercel Node function + Upstash Redis free tier, localStorage fallback), seeded with Legacy/ABC/SA rows, share-by-URL layouts
SA slotting optimiser (the 'AI opponent' beyond the required ABC baseline) with live objective curve, seed, iteration count and co-pick 'why' chips
Routing-policy ablation (S-shape, largest-gap, optimal) in Analytics
Picker handheld view (/handheld) mirroring the replay as an RF-gun pick list with next bay and metres to go
Exports: layout CSV/JSON, per-order replay CSV, KPI JSON, 3D snapshot PNG
In-app Methods panel printing data-cleaning counts, geometry, speeds, split and limitations
data_plan: Dataset: Online Retail II, UCI Machine Learning Repository id 502, CC BY 4.0; cite Chen, D. (2019), Online Retail II, UCI ML Repository, https://doi.org/10.24432/C5CG6D. Obtain via the Hugging Face parquet mirror verified tonight: curl -L -o online_retail_II.parquet "https://huggingface.co/datasets/vancevo/online-retail-ii/resolve/main/data/train-00000-of-00001.parquet" (7,156,732 B; 1,067,371 rows = exactly UCI's published count; columns Invoice, StockCode, Description, Quantity, InvoiceDate, Price, Customer_ID, Country; dates 2009-12-01 to 2011-12-09; Quantity and Price are stored as strings in this mirror, cast with pd.to_numeric). Fallback: Kaggle anonymous zip https://www.kaggle.com/api/v1/datasets/download/mashlyn/online-retail-ii-uci (15.2 MB) or the UCI xlsx (slow from campus). Month: November 2011 (3,021 non-cancelled invoices, the second-busiest month; Nov 2010 has 3,093 but 2011 is the same calendar year as the data's end and the deck can say 'peak season'). Preprocessing (data/prep.py, pandas 3.0.6 + pyarrow 26.0.0, Python 3.12, run with -I against the downloaded file): filter month -> drop 1,368 duplicate rows -> drop 441 cancelled invoices (1,073 rows) -> drop 283 non-product rows by regex ^\d{5}[A-Za-z]{0,2}$ (POST, DOT, M, C2, BANK CHARGES, DCGSSGIRL) -> drop 261 rows with Quantity<=0 or Price<=0 -> 80,378 pick lines / 2,751 orders / 2,933 SKUs -> top-100 SKUs by pick-line count -> 2,359 orders, 17,037 lines, coverage 21.2 % (displayed everywhere; 85.7 % of November orders touch at least one top-100 SKU). Chronological split: optimisation half Nov 1-15 (1,130 orders) used by the player and the SA optimiser; held-out half Nov 16-30 (1,229 orders) used for the final score, the leaderboard and the README table. Both halves are reported side by side. Legacy layout declared as catalogue order (StockCode ascending). Layout parameters (ours, stated in README and Methods panel): 5 aisles x 2 sides x 10 bays, bay pitch 1.2 m, aisle width 3.0 m, rack depth 1.0 m, cross-aisles 3.0 m, dock front-left, walking 1.2 m/s, 8 s per pick line, 15 s per order at dock; citations: Tompkins et al. 2010 (travel ~50 % of picker time), De Koster, Le-Duc & Roodbergen 2007 (order-picking review), Hall 1993 (S-shape/largest-gap), Ratliff & Rosenthal 1983 (optimal single-block routing, cited as not implemented). Committed artefacts: data/README.md (source, licence, command, counts), public/data/orders_2011-11.json (<1 MB), eval/results.md (generated by `npm run eval`, includes commit hash and date). No personal data: Customer_ID is dropped at prep time.
architecture: Single Vite 8 + React 19 + TypeScript SPA deployed as a static site on Vercel Hobby (zero cold start), plus ONE optional Vercel Node 22 serverless function api/leaderboard.ts (imports ../src/sim, re-simulates submitted layouts, stores scores in Upstash Redis via REST; env UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL/TOKEN in Vercel only, .env.example committed; if env missing the function returns 503 and the UI falls back to localStorage). Offline step: data/prep.py produces public/data/orders_2011-11.json. Client components: src/sim (layout.ts geometry + graph, dijkstra.ts all-pairs, routing.ts DP/2-opt/S-shape/largest-gap, simulate.ts, slotting.ts legacy/ABC/SA, batching.ts, multipicker.ts, prng.ts mulberry32, index.ts) shared with workers and the API; src/workers/sa.worker.ts (SA with progress messages) and src/workers/replay.worker.ts (multi-picker time-stepped runs); src/store.ts (zustand: data, layouts {legacy, abc, sa, player}, replay clock, settings, results cache keyed by layout hash + policy + params); src/scene/* (R3F Floor view: Racks, Bays, FloorHeat, PickerRig, PathLine, GhostRig, CameraRig, Post, PerfGuard); src/studio/* (2D slot map SVG, drag/swap, KPI panel, SA panel, why-chips); src/analytics/* (ECharts tables/charts, exports); src/handheld/* (phone frame route); src/leaderboard/*; src/methods/* (assumptions and counts). Data flow: JSON -> store -> simulate() (main thread, ms) -> results cache -> 3D traces + KPIs + charts; SA/multipicker -> workers -> store. Rendering runs entirely in the browser; no server compute except the leaderboard validation. Eval: eval/run.ts (tsx) runs every table and writes eval/results.md; vitest tests for graph distances on a toy 2-aisle layout, DP vs brute force on 7 stops, determinism, permutation validation. Repo: README.md (12 sections per judge checklist), DEV_LOG.md, .env.example, LICENSE MIT, docs/architecture.md (Mermaid), docs/pitch/SlotCraft_NexAI2026.pptx, docs/demo/script.md, data/, eval/, api/, src/, public/. CI: GitHub Actions running vitest + build on push.

build_plan:
Timeline IST, kickoff of build 21:45 on 21 Oct, feature freeze 11:00 on 22 Oct, submit 14:45. Four coding agents in parallel on branches, merged to main hourly by Agent D; humans own README prose, deck, recording, posts, and must read every merged file (code is kept boring: no frameworks beyond R3F/zustand).

Agent A, Simulation + data + eval (9.5 h): 21:45-23:15 data/prep.py + JSON + data/README.md with the real counts (first commit of data must land before any optimiser commit); 23:15-01:00 layout.ts, dijkstra.ts, routing.ts (Held-Karp, NN+2-opt+Or-opt, S-shape, largest-gap), simulate.ts, slotting.ts (legacy, ABC), vitest tests, eval/run.ts producing the first results.md; 01:00-04:00 sa.worker.ts with incremental delta and merged stop-sets, batching.ts (FCFS, savings), multipicker.ts (time-stepped congestion); 04:00-06:30 full eval tables (both halves, ablation, batching, congestion, 3 SA seeds), determinism test, README Evaluation and Data sections draft; 06:30-07:15 API validation helper for Agent C.

Agent B, 3D Floor view (9.5 h): 21:45-23:30 Vite scaffold (shared with C), R3F canvas, racks/bays instanced from layout.ts, dock, camera presets, perf guard, deployed walking skeleton by 23:30 (judges' progress review bait); 23:30-02:00 PickerRig following sim polylines, PathLine growing slice, counters bound to cumulative arrays, order ticker, bay hover/click card, speed control; 02:00-04:30 heat instanceColor for bays and floor tiles, Bloom/N8AO/SMAA with Performance Mode and auto-downgrade, ghost-race rig; 04:30-07:00 multi-picker rigs with congestion ring/labels and aisle tint, batching cart tags, snapshot PNG export, DPR cap, demand frameloop when paused.

Agent C, Studio / Analytics / Handheld / Leaderboard (9.5 h): 21:45-23:30 app shell, routes (Floor, Studio, Analytics, Handheld, Leaderboard, Methods), zustand store, data loader, results cache; 23:30-02:00 Studio 2D slot map (SVG, drag + click-to-swap, motion layout animations), KPI panel Legacy/ABC/You on both halves, undo/redo, share-by-URL hash; 02:00-04:30 SA panel (worker progress curve, seed, iterations, why-chips from co-pick matrix), Analytics tab with ECharts (KPI bars, ablation, histogram, congestion line, batching chart), CSV/JSON exports, Methods panel reading meta from JSON; 04:30-07:00 api/leaderboard.ts + Upstash + rate limit + localStorage fallback, Leaderboard UI with seeded rows, /handheld phone view, toasts.

Agent D, DevOps / docs / deck (6 h spread): 21:45-22:15 public repo, README skeleton, .env.example, DEV_LOG.md, LICENSE, .gitignore, Vercel project linked, GitHub Action; every hour: merge branches, tag mvp-m1/m2/m3, update DEV_LOG timeline; 05:00-08:00 README 12 sections, architecture Mermaid, docs/demo/script.md, QR PNGs, python-pptx deck skeleton with screenshots; 08:00-09:30 gitleaks scan, licence/citation check, post templates.

Integration + QA (all agents, 07:00-11:00, ~3 h effective): merge, test on a 4-year-old laptop in Chrome and Edge (Performance Mode default decision), replay-twice determinism check in the UI, eval re-run and freeze (tag eval-frozen, commit hash into README), deploy smoke test from a phone on mobile data, record 30 s clips for posts, feature freeze 11:00.

Humans 11:00-14:45: 11:00-12:30 final README/DEV_LOG review and line-by-line code read for Q&A ownership; 12:30-13:30 record the 5-min demo (OBS, 1080p) and the 3-min YouTube cut; 13:30-14:15 LinkedIn + X posts with #NEXAI2026, YouTube upload; 14:15-14:45 final smoke test on another laptop; submit by 14:45.
risks: Average-laptop GPU stutter: ~6 draw calls total via InstancedMesh/Instances, Bloom/N8AO behind a Performance Mode toggle that defaults ON when navigator.hardwareConcurrency < 8 or FPS < 40 for 2 s, DPR capped at 1.5 (1.0 in perf mode), frameloop demand when paused; tested on a weak laptop before 09:00
Judge asks to replay the whole month live: scoring is headless (simulate() over all 2,359 orders in ~30-60 ms) and the badge says so; the animation is a window; `npm run eval` reproduces every number

Coverage looks low (21.2 % of pick lines): framed as the forward-pick area, printed on screen with 85.7 % of orders touching it, and the top-N is a prep.py flag so the README can show top-200 coverage as context
Held-Karp blow-up on 76-line orders: unique stops deduped by node, exact DP only <= 11 stops, 2-opt+Or-opt beyond, policy badge states it, ablation shows the gap

SA too slow in the worker: incremental delta via SKU->orders inverted index, merged identical stop-sets, time-box 8 s with iteration count shown, warm start from ABC so even 2k iterations beat ABC; eval reports 3 seeds mean+-sd
3D drag-and-drop fiddly on stage: click-to-swap is primary in the 2D Studio map, 3D click-swap secondary, drag optional; the demo path uses click-swap
Leaderboard function or Upstash fails: UI falls back to localStorage with a visible 'local only' badge, leaderboard pre-seeded with Legacy/ABC/SA rows, Node function cold start ~300 ms only
Determinism doubts: seeded mulberry32 for SA, pure-function sim, vitest asserts two runs byte-identical, a 'Replay again' click in the demo shows identical numbers

Congestion model challenged as unrealistic: stated as a conservative single-lane assumption in Methods and README, parameters exposed (aisle capacity, step), results labelled as model outputs not forecasts

Commit-cadence or pre-kickoff suspicion: repo created 21:45 with DEV_LOG noting 18:00-21:30 planning/data exploration (allowed by section 2), hourly merges by Agent D, eval/test-set commit precedes optimiser commits, no force-push

Data mirror provenance questioned: parquet row count 1,067,371 matches UCI, columns match, README cites UCI DOI and names the mirror; Kaggle/UCI fallbacks listed; Quantity/Price string dtype handled explicitly
Time overrun: must-haves (M1-M3 + ABC baseline + eval) are all scheduled before 02:00; every stretch is a separate module that can be dropped without touching the core
